Scope of Cancellation Policy

This policy applies to:

* Physical products ordered through the platform
* Services that explicitly allow cancellation

This policy does **not** apply to:

* Digital products once access is granted
* Customized or made-to-order items
* Products marked as “Non-Cancellable”

---

1 PreShipment Cancellation

Customers may cancel an order **before it is shipped** by:

* Logging into their account
* Navigating to **My Orders**
* Selecting the order and choosing “Cancel”

Pre-shipment cancellations are **free of charge**.

---

2 PostShipment Cancellation

Once an order has been shipped:

* Cancellation is **not permitted**
* Customers must follow the **Return and Refund Policy** instead

Shipment status is final once updated by the logistics partner.

---

Cancellation by Company

The company reserves the right to cancel an order under the following circumstances:

* Product is out of stock
* Pricing or listing errors are identified
* Payment verification fails
* Suspected fraudulent or unauthorized transactions
* Regulatory or compliance restrictions
* Delivery location is non-serviceable

Customers are notified promptly if an order is cancelled by the company.

---

1 CustomerInitiated Cancellation (PreShipment)

* Full refund is issued to the original payment method
* Refund initiation occurs within **3–5 business days**

---

2 CompanyInitiated Cancellation

* Full refund is issued automatically
* Refund is processed regardless of payment method used

---

Partial Cancellations

For orders containing multiple items:

* Customers may cancel individual items **before shipment**
* Shipped items cannot be partially cancelled

Refunds apply only to cancelled items.

---

Cancellation of Services

Cancellation terms for services vary and are:

* Clearly mentioned on the service detail page
* Subject to service-specific timelines and conditions

Service cancellations outside the allowed window may not be eligible for refunds.

---

NonCancellable Orders

Orders cannot be cancelled if:

* The order status is “Shipped” or “Out for Delivery”
* The product is customized or personalized
* The product is labeled as non-cancellable

Such orders must follow return or replacement procedures if applicable.

---

Failed Delivery Cancellations

If an order is returned due to:

* Multiple failed delivery attempts
* Incorrect address provided by the customer

The order may be cancelled automatically.

Refund eligibility depends on:

* Product type
* Return condition
* Reason for delivery failure

Shipping charges may be deducted where applicable.

---

Cancellation Confirmation

Upon successful cancellation:

* A confirmation message is sent via email or SMS
* Order status is updated in the user account

Lack of confirmation indicates the cancellation was not completed.

---

Disputes Related to Cancellation

Customers may raise disputes if:

* Refund is not received within the stated timeline
* Cancellation request was incorrectly rejected

Disputes must be raised within **14 days** of the cancellation decision.

---

Abuse of Cancellation Policy

The company reserves the right to:

* Restrict cancellation privileges
* Suspend accounts exhibiting repeated misuse or abuse

Such actions are taken after internal review.

---

Policy Modifications

The company may:

* Update this Cancellation Policy at any time
* Apply revised policies to future orders

The latest version is always available on the platform.

---

End of Cancellation Policy

---

Overview

Nvidia Corporation (/ɛnˈvɪdiə/ en-VID-ee-ə) is an American technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang (president and CEO), Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, it develops graphics processing units (GPUs), systems on chips (SoCs), and application programming interfaces (APIs) for data science, high-performance computing, and mobile and automotive applications.

Originally focused on GPUs for video gaming, Nvidia broadened their use into other markets, including artificial intelligence (AI), professional visualization, and supercomputing. The company's product lines include GeForce GPUs for gaming and creative workloads, and professional GPUs for edge computing, scientific research, and industrial applications. As of the first quarter of 2025, Nvidia held a 92% share of the discrete desktop and laptop GPU market.

Market Dominance and AI Boom

In the early 2000s, the company invested over a billion dollars to develop CUDA, a software platform and API that enabled GPUs to run massively parallel programs for a broad range of compute-intensive applications. As a result, as of 2025, Nvidia controlled more than 80% of the market for GPUs used in training and deploying AI models, and provided chips for over 75% of the world's TOP500 supercomputers.

In 2023, Nvidia became the seventh U.S. company to reach a US$1 trillion valuation. In 2025, it became the first to surpass US$4 trillion in market capitalization, driven by rising global demand for data center hardware in the midst of the AI boom. For its strength, size and market capitalization, Nvidia has been selected to be one of Bloomberg's "Magnificent Seven".

History

3.1 Founding (1993)

Nvidia was founded on April 5, 1993, by Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese-American electrical engineer previously at LSI Logic and AMD; Chris Malachowsky, an engineer from Sun Microsystems; and Curtis Priem, formerly of IBM and Sun Microsystems. In late 1992, the three men agreed to start the company in a meeting at a Denny's roadside diner on Berryessa Road in East San Jose.

The founders envisioned graphics-based processing as the best trajectory for tackling challenges that had eluded general-purpose computing methods. Video games served as their "killer app"—a flywheel to reach large markets funding huge R&D to solve massive computational problems. The company was born with $40,000 in the bank and subsequently received $20 million of venture capital funding from Sequoia Capital and others.

3.2 The Company Name

Nvidia initially had no name. Early ideas included "Primal Graphics," "Huaprimal," and "NVision" (which was already taken by a toilet paper manufacturer). The name "Nvidia" comes from "invidia," the Latin word for "envy."

3.3 First Graphics Accelerator (NV1)

Nvidia's first graphics accelerator, the NV1, was designed to process quadrilateral primitives. However, when Microsoft introduced DirectX, it chose to support only triangle primitives. Consequently, the NV1 failed to gain traction.

3.4 Partnership with Sega and Financial Crisis

Nvidia entered a partnership with Sega for the Dreamcast console but realized their technology was lagging. Sega's president, Shoichiro Irimajiri, decided to choose another vendor but persuaded Sega's management to invest $5 million into Nvidia. This funding "gave the company six months to live." In 1996, Huang laid off more than half the staff, focusing on a triangle-optimized product: the RIVA 128.

3.5 The Pivot and Public Offering (1999)

By August 1997, Nvidia had only enough money for one month's payroll. This gave rise to the unofficial motto: "Our company is thirty days from going out of business." However, Nvidia sold a million RIVA 128 units within four months.

Nvidia went public on January 22, 1999. Later that year, it released the GeForce 256 (NV10), marketed as the world's first GPU, introducing onboard transformation and lighting (T&L).

3.6 Acquisitions and Early 2000s Growth

2000: Acquired assets of rival 3dfx.

2001: Selected to replace Enron in the S&P 500.

2002: Acquired Exluna.

2003: Acquired MediaQ for $70 million.

2004: Assisted Sony with the PlayStation 3 graphics processor (RSX); acquired iReady.

2005: Acquired ULI Electronics.

2006: Acquired Hybrid Graphics.

Eras of Development

4.1 2007–2014: Diversification

In 2007, Forbes named Nvidia "Company of the Year." Acquisitions included PortalPlayer and Ageia (developer of the PhysX engine). During this era, the company faced class action lawsuits over "abnormal failure rates" in mobile chipsets, reaching a settlement in 2010.

2011: Released Tegra 3, the first quad-core mobile CPU.

2013: Unveiled Tegra 4 and the Nvidia Shield handheld console.

2014: Diversified into gaming, automotive electronics, and mobile devices.

4.2 2016–2018: Pascal and AI

Nvidia unveiled the GeForce 10 series based on the Pascal microarchitecture. Partnerships with Toyota and Baidu focused on AI platforms for autonomous vehicles.

2017: Released Titan V.

2018: Integrated Tesla P4 cards into Google Cloud AI; released RTX 2080.

Mac Driver Dispute: A rift formed between Apple and Nvidia regarding macOS Mojave drivers, leading to Apple users having to switch to AMD Radeon cards.

4.3 2019: Acquisition of Mellanox

Nvidia announced a $6.9 billion deal to buy Mellanox Technologies to expand its footprint in high-performance computing.

4.4 2020–2023: The AI Shift

2020: Acquired Cumulus Networks; announced the Ampere GPU architecture.

Arm Takeover Attempt: Nvidia announced a $40 billion deal to buy Arm from SoftBank, but the transaction was terminated in 2022 due to "significant regulatory challenges."

Infrastructure: Launched the Cambridge-1 supercomputer in 2021; opened new headquarters buildings "Endeavor" and "Voyager."

4.5 2024–2025: The Blackwell Era and $4 Trillion Mark

Blackwell: In March 2024, Nvidia announced the Blackwell microarchitecture.

Valuation Milestones: Surpassed $2 trillion in March 2024 and $4 trillion in July 2025.

DeepSeek Impact: In January 2025, Nvidia saw a $600 billion one-day loss in market cap after the Chinese AI startup DeepSeek released an advanced model at a significantly lower cost.

Global Demand: By late 2024, Morgan Stanley reported the entire 2025 production of Blackwell chips was sold out.

Business Operations

5.1 Fabless Manufacturing

Nvidia uses external suppliers (like TSMC) for all phases of manufacturing (wafer fabrication, assembly, and testing). This allows the company to focus resources on product design, quality assurance, and marketing.

5.2 Leadership

Jensen Huang: Founder, President, and CEO

5.3 Board of Directors

The board includes notable figures like Rob Burgess, Tench Coxe, John Dabiri, Persis Drell, Dawn Hudson, Ellen Ochoa, and Mark Stevens.

Products and Ecosystem

6.1 Product Families

GeForce: Consumer graphics

RTX: Professional visual computing (replacing Quadro)

Tegra: SoCs for mobile devices

Tesla/Datacenter: GPUs for scientific fields (A100, H100)

Grace: Datacenter/server CPU

Drive: Autonomous vehicle hardware/software

BlueField: Data processing units (DPUs)

Shield: Gaming hardware range

6.2 GPU Technology Conference (GTC)

GTC is a series of technical conferences started in 2009. Originally focused on GPUs, it has shifted to AI, deep learning, and self-driving cars.

6.3 Deep Learning and Robotics

DGX: A line of supercomputers for deep learning.

Omniverse: A virtual environment for engineers.

Isaac Sim: Simulations for training robots.

Isaac GR00T N1: An open-source foundation model for humanoid robots.

OpenSource Software Support

Historically, Nvidia did not publish documentation for its hardware, causing tension with the Linux community (famously criticized by Linus Torvalds). However, in 2022, Nvidia began open-sourcing GPU kernel modules. In 2025, they announced CUDA support for RISC-V.

Controversies

8.1 Maxwell Advertising (GTX 970)

Users discovered the GTX 970 could only access 3.5 GB of its 4 GB VRAM at high speeds. This led to a class-action lawsuit and a $30 refund for purchasers.

8.2 GeForce Partner Program

A controversial marketing program canceled in 2018 amid anti-competitive practice complaints.

8.3 Hardware Unboxed Dispute

In 2020, Nvidia briefly banned a tech reviewer for focusing on rasterization instead of ray tracing, but quickly reversed the decision and apologized.

8.4 SEC and Cryptomining

Nvidia paid $5.5 million in 2022 to settle charges that it failed to disclose how much of its gaming revenue growth was driven by cryptomining.

8.5 Geopolitical Issues

China Export Restrictions: U.S. embargoes on advanced chips led Nvidia to create China-specific chips (A800, H20).

H20 Production Halt: In August 2025, Nvidia halted H20 production after Chinese government warnings to domestic firms regarding security concerns.

Shanghai Facility: A proposed facility in Shanghai faced criticism from U.S. senators over national security issues.

8.6 AI Regulation Dispute

In 2025, a public dispute occurred between Jensen Huang and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei regarding AI regulation and industry "safety" concerns.

Scope of the Refund Policy

This policy applies to:

* Physical products purchased through the platform
* Select services explicitly marked as refundable

This policy does **not** apply to:

* Digital goods once accessed or downloaded
* Gift cards, vouchers, or promotional credits
* Items explicitly labeled as **“Non-Refundable”**

---

Eligibility Criteria for Refund

A refund request may be approved if **any one** of the following conditions is met:

1 Defective or Damaged Items

* The product is physically damaged at the time of delivery
* The product has manufacturing defects affecting usability

Evidence such as photos or videos may be required.

---

2 Incorrect Item Delivered

* A different product than what was ordered is delivered
* Incorrect size, color, or variant is delivered

The item must remain unused and in original condition.

---

3 Item Not as Described

* The product significantly differs from the description on the product page
* Key features or specifications are missing or incorrect

Minor variations in color or packaging do not qualify.

---

4 NonDelivery or Late Delivery

* The order is not delivered within the promised delivery timeline
* The shipment is marked delivered but not received by the customer

Verification with the logistics partner may be required.

---

NonRefundable Scenarios

Refunds will **not** be issued in the following cases:

* Change of mind after delivery
* Incorrect address provided by the customer
* Damage caused by misuse, negligence, or improper handling
* Products returned without original packaging or accessories
* Requests raised after the eligible refund window

---

Refund Request Timeline

Customers must initiate a refund request within the following periods:

 Standard products : Within **7 days** of delivery 
 Perishable / consumable items : Within **48 hours** of delivery 
 Services : As specified on the service page 

Requests submitted outside these timelines may be automatically rejected.

---

Refund Request Process

To request a refund, customers must:

Submit required supporting evidence (if applicable)

Once submitted, the request enters review status.

---

Review and Approval Process

* Refund requests are reviewed within **2–4 business days**
* Additional verification may be requested
* The company reserves the right to approve or reject requests based on policy compliance

Decisions are communicated via email or in-app notification.

---

Refund Method

Approved refunds are processed using one of the following methods:

* Original payment method (preferred)
* Store credit (if original method is unavailable or expired)

Refunds **cannot** be redirected to a different bank account or payment method upon request.

---

Refund Processing Time

After approval:

* Refunds are initiated within **5–7 business days**
* Bank or payment provider processing may take an additional **3–5 business days**

The company is not responsible for delays caused by banks or payment gateways.

---

Partial Refunds

Partial refunds may be issued in cases where:

* Only part of the order qualifies for refund
* Returned items show signs of use
* Accessories, manuals, or packaging are missing

The refund amount is determined after inspection.

---

Inspection of Returned Items

For returns requiring physical pickup:

* Items undergo inspection upon receipt
* Refund approval is contingent on inspection outcome
* Inspection failure may result in refund rejection or reduced refund

---

Rejected Refund Requests

If a refund request is rejected:

* The reason for rejection will be communicated
* The item may be returned to the customer
* No refund will be processed

---

Dispute Resolution

Customers may dispute a refund decision by:

* Contacting customer support within **14 days** of rejection
* Providing additional clarification or evidence

Decisions after dispute review are final.

---

Policy Modifications

The company reserves the right to:

* Modify this Refund Policy at any time
* Apply updated terms to future purchases

The latest version will always be available on the platform.

---

End of Refund Policy

---

1 Domestic Shipping

We ship products to all **serviceable domestic locations** supported by our logistics partners.

Delivery availability depends on:

* Product type
* Delivery address
* Pin code serviceability

---

2 International Shipping

International shipping is available only for:

* Selected products
* Selected countries

International shipping availability is displayed on the product page or at checkout.

---

Order Processing Time

* Orders are processed within **24–48 business hours** after successful payment confirmation.
* Orders placed on **weekends or public holidays** are processed on the next business day.
* Processing time does **not** include shipping or delivery time.

Orders requiring manual verification or customization may take longer.

---

Shipping Methods

Available shipping methods may include:

* Standard Shipping
* Express Shipping (if supported for the location and product)

The available method and estimated delivery timeline are shown during checkout.

---

Estimated Delivery Time

Estimated delivery timelines are as follows:

 Standard Shipping is done in **3–7 business days** 
 Express Shipping is done in **1–3 business days** 

Delivery timelines are **estimates only** and may vary due to external factors.

---

Shipping Charges

* Shipping charges, if applicable, are clearly displayed at checkout before payment.
* Free shipping may be offered:

 * On orders above a specified value
 * During promotional periods

Shipping charges are **non-refundable** once the order is shipped.

---

Shipment Tracking

* Once an order is shipped, a **tracking ID** is generated.
* Tracking details are shared via:

 * Email
 * SMS
 * Order details page

Tracking updates depend on the logistics partner and may not be real-time.

---

Delivery Attempts

* Delivery partners typically attempt delivery **up to 2–3 times**.
* If delivery fails due to:

 * Customer unavailability
 * Incorrect address
 * Incomplete contact details

The shipment may be returned to origin.

---

Delayed Deliveries

Delays may occur due to:

* Weather conditions
* Natural disasters
* Logistics disruptions
* Regulatory restrictions
* High demand periods (sales, festivals)

The company is not liable for delays caused by factors beyond its control.

---

1 Undelivered Orders

If an order is not delivered within the estimated timeframe:

* Customers may contact support
* An investigation with the logistics partner is initiated

---

2 Lost Shipments

If a shipment is confirmed as lost:

* A replacement or refund may be issued
* Resolution is subject to verification and internal review

---

Delivery Confirmation

Delivery is considered complete when:

* The product is marked as delivered by the logistics partner
* The product is handed over at the delivery address

The company is not responsible for loss after confirmed delivery.

---

Address Accuracy

Customers are responsible for providing:

* Correct delivery address
* Accurate contact details

Orders delivered to incorrect addresses due to customer error are not eligible for refunds.

---

Damaged Packages During Delivery

If the outer package appears damaged:

* Customers are advised to inspect before accepting delivery
* Any visible damage should be reported immediately

Acceptance of delivery indicates the package was received in acceptable condition.

---

Shipping Restrictions

Certain products may be subject to:

* Regional restrictions
* Regulatory shipping limitations
* Carrier-specific constraints

Such restrictions are communicated at checkout where applicable.

---

Policy Changes

The company reserves the right to:

* Update or modify this Shipping Policy at any time
* Apply revised terms to future orders

The latest version will be published on the platform.

---

End of Shipping Policy
